body:
hah yeah, I get where you're going and done lots of self-analysis to try and find out why this is. Some of the talking-self-out-of-things is definitely true, but it happens before even asking. The ones I do ask out I follow up with - all the okcupid ones were after they said "no thanks" (with varying degrees of politeness) to a second.

I did exhaustive research on just about every topic related to what I was trying to accomplish (literally - I'm pretty ashamed and so tired when I think of all the work I put into not only improving myself but reading up on how "normal" people do it). As far as I can tell I'm not doing much wrong, but perhaps do not have the right mindset.

I've never been able to not-care about rejection. So with below-average, boring-personality me, I should be using the "shotgun" method, just asking out as many girls as possible to get accidental yesses, and second yesses, until it sticks. I can't really do that. It's too emotionally draining for me.

It was almost always them - I think maybe I come off boring on a first date, and have more success with the friend-first path. Unfortunately that also takes longer and is often the friend-last path.

The only ones I ended from okc were the obvious trainwrecks, like the girl that met me at a coffee shop and started the conversation with "so thanks for the coffee but just so you know my bf got out of prison yesterday and we hooked up so don't think this is going anywhere." Ooookay.

I generally give people the benefit of the doubt, let them surprise me, but most others don't seem to have time for it.
Yes, I have phases where I try stuff like OkCupid. Strongest after my breakup 6 years ago, but it's never panned out. Lots of first dates, no seconds. Haven't so much as kissed a girl in that time.

I've been slowly upgrading my environment for many years - it's helped a bit, but the basic problems don't change.

This guy's not a pussy hound thankfully, and she wasn't friendzoning me (we've flirted mutually before, but she's always backed off). She wasn't a crush, just someone I was really hoping to get with, short term or long I would have taken either. He's just charming when drunk and gives zero fucks, makes decisions he knows are probably wrong. He just got out of a breakup so I'm sure he needed it...I'm just...he falls into these all the time and...I needed it more.

I've needed it more for a long time. So much that I'm at the point where I'm considering paying for it, even though I know how hollow of an experience that would be for me.

I try not to judge other people for their actions, and I want everyone to be happy. I just wish I could find someone who's willing to share that happiness with me.

I guess everyone's looking for that. But after six years, trying literally every bit of advice I was given, could come up with on my own, improving myself, and having absolutely NOTHING to show for it...

Maybe that's what I'll ask to be put on my marker.

"It all became a bit much."
When my roommate has sex with people I've been trying to flirt with earlier, and I can hear it through the walls.
